description:
Found while building the Map surface for fz-5xp.12. A LIMIT to record, not a
bug to fix.

    Map.keys(%{a: 1, b: 2, c: 3})
      elixir  [:c, :a, :b]
      fz      [:a, :b, :c]

Elixir's order here is stable across runs and independent of the literal's
order -- `%{c: 3, b: 2, a: 1}` gives the same `[:c, :a, :b]` -- but it is
neither alphabetical (`%{zz: 1, aa: 2}` gives `[:zz, :aa]`) nor creation order.
It is Erlang's internal atom identity, which fz cannot reproduce because fz
interns its own atoms with its own ids.

BINARY keys are different and DO match: Elixir orders them by content, and
fz-5xp.48 made fz do the same. `Map.keys(%{"b" => 1, "a" => 2})` is `["a", "b"]`
in both.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ORACLES. A fixture whose twin prints an atom-keyed map's
iteration order will diverge, and no amount of work on fz's side fixes it.
Fixtures must either use binary keys where order is printed, or sort before
printing, or not print order.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GOAL PROGRAM: none. JSON object keys are strings, so
`Json.decode` builds BINARY-keyed maps, which are exactly the case that matches.

Related: fz renders `%{:a => 1}` where Elixir renders `%{a: 1}` -- the atom-key
shorthand. That one IS fixable and is a separate ticket.
title: Atom-keyed map iteration order cannot match Elixir
